description: The interface languages (acceptance test A5: a new language needs only translation files): each language's own name, the locale its numbers and dates are written in, its BCP-47 tag, its writing direction and what its built file says about it. The source language is the English every key falls back to. A language is added here and as a column of every data/i18n/strings/*.txt file (named in the file's #!columns header); scripts/i18n/build-i18n.mjs then writes its files and the runtime (site/assets/i18n/i18n.js) and the shared formatter (packages/core/src/format.js) follow it with no code change. Schema: packages/registries/schemas/languages.schema.json; views: packages/registries/src/languages.mjs.

en.name: English
en.role: source and fallback for every key

ga.name: Gaeilge
ga.terminology: téarma.ie (National Terminology Database for Irish, © Foras na Gaeilge) for administrative, electoral and computing terms; individual terms used, the database is not reproduced

sco.name: Ulstèr-Scotch
sco.localeNote: BCP-47 'sco' (ISO 639-3 Scots) with the IANA variant subtag 'ulster' (registered 2010). Intl has no Scots locale data, so Ulster-Scots writes numbers and dates as en-GB.
sco.standard: none settled; conservative forms only, from published official usage where found (NI Assembly Ulster-Scots leaflet, NISRA census leaflet, Ulster-Scots Agency / Tha Boord o Ulstèr-Scotch); otherwise English is kept
